source: Commercial listing snapshot from Crexi, LoopNet, Showcase and prior Zillow watchlist
disclaimer: Listing status, price, zoning, utilities, access, traffic claims and development feasibility must be independently verified with the broker and public agencies. Scores are planning proxies, not investment advice. Some map coordinates are approximate corridor locations.

listings.status: Active ground lease — broker rate required
listings.zoning: Commercial retail use advertised; verify parcel zoning
listings.traffic: Listing highlights heavy traffic, approximately 120 feet of Kolb frontage, cross access and a location just off the hard corner.
listings.note: A roughly 0.25-acre ground-lease pad is explicitly offered for an efficiently designed drive-through building. The center is anchored by Chuze Fitness, Goodwill, D2 and Popeyes, with Chipotle identified for the hard corner. This avoids a land purchase above the $200,000 cap, but the lease rate, annual escalations, delivery condition, utility stubs, stacking geometry, exclusivity and landlord contribution must be confirmed before treating it as affordable.

listings.address: NEC and SWC of Kolb Rd & Valencia Rd, Tucson, AZ 85756
listings.traffic: Listing reports approximately 79,000 vehicles per day at a signalized intersection.
listings.note: Retail and industrial pads range from about 69,062 to 193,373 square feet. Signalized access, monument-signage availability, nearby employment hubs and southeast residential growth make this the strongest current active lead. Confirm which pad is C-2, whether drive-through stacking is permitted and the seller's minimum pad price.

listings.traffic: I-10 interchange exposure; broker materials cite nearby Amazon, UA Science & Tech Park and La Estancia demand generators.
listings.note: Available pads are advertised from approximately 0.84 to 2.2 acres, which is much closer to the footprint needed for a compact drive-through than buying the entire tract. This is a strong growth-corridor candidate, but the morning beverage trade area and price must be compared with the more established Speedway/Kolb area.

listings.traffic: Listing reports more than 70,000 AADT, multiple access points and Speedway exposure.
listings.note: This 14,047-square-foot paved pad has utilities on site and is marketed for retail or restaurant use. It is almost exactly the kind of compact site SNAP needs, and City records show a prior pre-application for a new structure with drive-through and patio. It is currently under contract, so treat it as the benchmark site and ask the broker whether backup offers are accepted.

listings.traffic: Listing reports more than 84,000 vehicles per day and access from both Kolb Road and Valencia Road.
listings.note: The price, acreage and dual-road access create a stronger land-investment case than a first-store case. Industrial zoning may not support the intended retail beverage use without additional approvals, and 5.2 acres is far more land than one SNAP unit needs. Do not buy this only for the store unless a subdivision, ground lease or broader development plan is proven.

listings.traffic: Direct I-10 frontage and interchange exposure near La Estancia, Amazon, Port of Tucson and UA Science & Tech Park.
listings.note: This is an institutional-size 16.42-acre opportunity rather than a practical first-store purchase. Only pursue it if the owner will sell or ground-lease a small pad, or if the thesis expands into a multi-tenant commercial development.

listings.address: 1930 E Old Vail Connection Rd, Tucson, AZ 85756
listings.note: One-acre parcel on a named connection road. Strong candidate for access, utility and commercial-use verification.

listings.address: 485 S Hotel Service Rd, Tucson, AZ 85745
listings.note: Large service-road parcel with potential visibility. Price and site-work burden require deeper diligence.
One-acre north-side parcel at a comparatively moderate asking price. Verify commercial use and ingress.
Large acreage for the price on a major road. Better initial land-hold candidate until utilities and zoning are confirmed.

listings.address: 6171 W Irvington Rd Unit 4, Tucson, AZ 85757
listings.note: Nearly three acres on an arterial. Attractive price-per-acre, but operating demand and infrastructure need validation.
Urban location near key demand areas, but the parcel may be too constrained for a conventional drive-through.

listings.address: 7875 E River Forest Pl #1, Tucson, AZ 85715
listings.note: Half-acre east-side parcel. Could fit a compact format if access, visibility and commercial use are viable.
Affordable infill parcel. More likely a walk-up or hold candidate than a full drive-through without assemblage.
Low asking price on a major corridor, but the small lot may only support a micro-format or assemblage.
Compact infill parcel with central access. Drive-through geometry is uncertain.
Low-cost infill parcel. Better as a land-watch candidate unless commercial access and use are confirmed.
Urban parcel near demand generators, but likely too small for a standard drive-through configuration.
